problem:
Let $Z$ be a random variable with a continuous distribution having density
$$
f_{Z}(z)=\begin{cases}
2z & \text{if } 0 \leq z \leq 1 \\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two random variables, independent given $Z=z$, satisfying
$$
\mathbf{P}(X=1 \mid Z=z)=z=1-\mathbf{P}(X=0 \mid Z=z)
$$
and
$$
\mathbf{P}(Y=1 \mid Z=z)=z=1-\mathbf{P}(Y=0 \mid Z=z)
$$
Find the conditional probability
$$
\mathbf{P}(Z \leq 1/2 \mid X=1 \text{ and } Y=1).
$$

answer_text:
We want

\[
\mathbf{P}\!\left(Z\le \frac12 \mid X=1,\;Y=1\right).
\]

Since \(Z\) has density \(f_Z(z)=2z\) on \([0,1]\), and given \(Z=z\), the variables \(X\) and \(Y\) are independent with

\[
\mathbf{P}(X=1\mid Z=z)=z,\qquad 
\mathbf{P}(Y=1\mid Z=z)=z,
\]

we have

\[
\mathbf{P}(X=1,Y=1\mid Z=z)=z^2.
\]

By Bayes’ rule,

\[
\mathbf{P}\!\left(Z\le \frac12 \mid X=1,Y=1\right)
=
\frac{\mathbf{P}\!\left(Z\le \frac12,\;X=1,Y=1\right)}
{\mathbf{P}(X=1,Y=1)}.
\]

Using the law of total probability,

\[
\mathbf{P}\!\left(Z\le \frac12,\;X=1,Y=1\right)
=
\int_0^{1/2} \mathbf{P}(X=1,Y=1\mid Z=z) f_Z(z)\,dz.
\]

Thus,

\[
\mathbf{P}\!\left(Z\le \frac12,\;X=1,Y=1\right)
=
\int_0^{1/2} z^2(2z)\,dz
=
2\int_0^{1/2} z^3\,dz.
\]

Similarly,

\[
\mathbf{P}(X=1,Y=1)
=
\int_0^1 z^2(2z)\,dz
=
2\int_0^1 z^3\,dz.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\mathbf{P}\!\left(Z\le \frac12 \mid X=1,Y=1\right)
=
\frac{2\int_0^{1/2} z^3\,dz}{2\int_0^1 z^3\,dz}.
\]

Compute the integrals:

\[
\int_0^{1/2} z^3\,dz
=
\left[\frac{z^4}{4}\right]_0^{1/2}
=
\frac{(1/2)^4}{4}
=
\frac{1}{64},
\]

and

\[
\int_0^1 z^3\,dz
=
\left[\frac{z^4}{4}\right]_0^1
=
\frac14.
\]

Hence,

\[
\mathbf{P}\!\left(Z\le \frac12 \mid X=1,Y=1\right)
=
\frac{2\cdot \frac{1}{64}}{2\cdot \frac14}
=
\frac{1/64}{1/4}
=
\frac14 \cdot \frac{1}{16}
=
\frac1{16}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{16}}
\]
